gap: No result ChatGPT got states the hard-drive limit that decides whether a 12 V NAS can be wired to a van's house battery. NAS drives are specified at 12 V ±10% (10.8–13.2 V). A 12 V LiFePO4 bank charges at up to 14.6 V, which is 1.4 V above that limit. So a 12 V-input NAS needs a regulated DC-DC converter set to 12 V, such as Victron's Orion-Tr 12/12, which accepts 8–17 V in and gives an adjustable 10–15 V out.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited. QNAP's TS-233 hardware specs say only 'Minimum 48W adapter (12VDC), 100-240VAC' and give 10.81 W typical and 3.43 W disk standby. The Synology DS124/DS223j and DS223/DS223j compare pages give adapter wattage (36 W, 60 W), 100–240 V AC input and access/hibernation watts, with no DC output voltage or tolerance. No cited page gives a DC input tolerance. ChatGPT's own answer did say a van bus runs about 11–14.6 V and told the shopper to use a fused, regulated DC-DC converter. But it never gave the drive-side limit (13.2 V) that explains why, or a converter that can be set to 12 V. So this adds the reason and the number, not the advice itself.
decides: This confirms the plan rather than changing which NAS to buy. Every 2-bay candidate (QNAP TS-233, Synology DS124/DS223j, UGREEN DH2300/DXP2800) runs from a 12 V brick, so all of them work in a van, but only behind a regulated 12 V DC-DC converter, not wired straight to the house battery. During charging (14.6 V from a LiFePO4 charger like Redodo's) the bus is 1.4 V, or about 11%, above the 13.2 V ceiling the drives are specified for. The converter's own losses add to the NAS's spec-sheet watts in the Ah/day column. The 19–20 V UGREEN models (DXP4800 Plus, DXP480T Plus) need a boost converter anyway. An all-SSD build doesn't avoid the issue, because SATA SSDs take 5 V from the NAS's own regulator.

findings.label: 3.5-inch NAS hard drive 12 V supply tolerance (Seagate IronWolf spec)
findings.source_title: Seagate IronWolf HDD 10TB Review - StorageReview.com (Lyle Smith, 2016-11-20)
findings.note: StorageReview's spec table quotes 'Voltage Tolerance (12V): ±10%' and 'Voltage Tolerance (5V): ±5%'. 12 × 1.10 = 13.2 V maximum. Seagate's own datasheet and manual PDFs would not decode to text, so this is the named reviewer's copy of Seagate's spec.

findings.label: 3.5-inch NAS hard drive 12 V spin-up current (Seagate IronWolf)
findings.value: 1.8 A (10 TB), 2.0 A (2–8 TB), 1.2 A (1 TB), typical at 12 V
findings.source_title: Seagate IronWolf HDD 10TB Review - StorageReview.com (Lyle Smith, 2016-11-20)
findings.note: Two drives spinning up at once draw about 4 A = about 48 W at 12 V. That matches QNAP's 'minimum 48W adapter' and is why a converter has to be sized for startup, not the 10.8 W typical draw.

findings.label: Charging voltage of a 12 V LiFePO4 house battery
findings.note: Maker's text: 'The output voltage is up to 14.6V'. 14.6 − 13.2 = 1.4 V (about 11%) above the drive's 12 V ceiling while charging. $82.99 on redodopower.com on 2026-11-17 (list $119.99).

findings.label: Regulated 12 V supply from a van battery: Victron Orion-Tr 12/12 isolated
findings.value: input 8–17 V; output adjustable 10–15 V; no-load input current < 80 mA; standby < 1 mA
findings.source_title: Victron Energy, Orion-Tr Smart DC-DC Charger Isolated manual, 8. Specifications
findings.note: The 8–17 V input covers the 14.6 V charging peak, and the output can be set to 12.0 V. The < 80 mA no-load draw is about 1 W of overhead at 12.8 V (about 23 Ah/day if left on with no load, an upper bound), before conversion losses.

findings.label: Power input and draw
findings.value: Minimum 48 W adapter (12 V DC), 100–240 V AC; 10.81 W operating (typical, drives fully populated); 3.43 W disk standby
findings.note: No DC input tolerance published. 10.81 W ÷ 12 V = 0.9 A; 0.9 A × 24 h ≈ 21.6 Ah/day before converter losses.

findings.value: 60 W adapter, 100–240 V AC; 16.31 W access; 4 W HDD hibernation
findings.source_title: Synology Inc. product compare DS124 / DS223j
findings.note: Synology does not state the adapter's DC output voltage on this page.
